subject: AI & Agents
title: Regression: Predicting a Number
description: One-minute skill: Regression: Predicting a Number.

hook.text: How much will your house sell for? AI doesn't guess — it calculates from patterns.

buildup.text: Regression models predict continuous values — prices, temperatures, stock returns.

discovery.text: They find the mathematical relationship between inputs and a numerical outcome.

twist.text: A model predicting used car prices learned that red cars sell for more — because sports cars are red.

climax.text: Correlation isn't causation, but regression models can't tell the difference.

punchline.text: It finds the trend line. You decide if it matters.

quiz.question: What does a regression model predict?

details.summary: Regression predicts a continuous number rather than a category — like predicting house prices, temperature, or stock returns. It is one of AI's simplest and most widely used prediction techniques.
details.whyItMatters: Regression models drive real-world decisions in finance, healthcare, and engineering. Understanding how they estimate numbers helps evaluate when their predictions are trustworthy.
takeaways: Regression predicts continuous numerical values from input features
It is used for price prediction, forecasting, and risk estimation
Simple regression often outperforms complex models for clean data

faq.question: What is the difference between regression and classification?
faq.answer: Classification predicts a category: spam or not spam. Regression predicts a number: what will the house sell for? Both are supervised learning, but regression outputs continuous values instead of discrete categories.

faq.question: When should you use simple regression versus complex models?
faq.answer: Simple linear regression works well when relationships are straightforward and data is clean. Complex models like neural networks help when relationships are highly non-linear, but need more data to avoid overfitting.
